French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • ognon (post-1990 spelling)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French oingnon, from Old French oignon, from Latin ūniōnem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (France) IPA(key): /ɔ.ɲɔ̃/, (proscribed but common) /wa.ɲɔ̃/
    • Audio; “un oignon”:(file)
    • (Provence) IPA(key): /oˈɲɔᵑ/, /oˈɲɔŋ/
  • (Canada) IPA(key): /ɔɲõ/
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Massy)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

oignon m (plural oignons)

  1. onion (Allium cepa)
    • 2025 May 21, “Il commande un hamburger sans oignon, mais en reçoit quand même: un Américain réclame 1 million de dommages et intérêts”, in rtl.be‎[1]:
      Un client américain avait demandé un burger sans oignons à cause de son allergie. Servi malgré tout avec l’ingrédient indésirable, il a fini aux urgences et poursuit ainsi la chaîne de fast-food pour négligence grave.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  2. bulb (of a plant)
  3. (in the plural, colloquial) one's own business

Derived terms

[edit]
  • aux petits oignons
  • en rang d'oignon
  • oignon vert
  • se mêler de ses oignons, s'occuper de ses oignons (“mind one's own business”)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Saint Dominican Creole French: z'oignon
    • Haitian Creole: zonyon
  • Seychellois Creole: zonyon

Further reading

[edit]
  • “oignon”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
Alternative forms
  • hoinnon, hoynon, hoynoun, hoynun, hoynune, hunion, oignion, oignoun, oignun, oingnon, oingnun, oingoun, oinion, oiniun, oinoin, oinon, oinoun, oinum, oinun, oinunne, oissnion, ongnion, ongnon, ongnun, onion, onyon, oygnon, oygnoun, oygnun, oyngnoun, oyngon, oynnun, oynoin, oynon, oynoun, oynun, oynune, ugnon, ugnoun, ungeon, ungnun, union, unioun, uniun, unniun, unon

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin ūniōnem.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (classical) IPA(key): /uˈɲun/

Noun

[edit]

oignon oblique singular, m (oblique plural oignons, nominative singular oignons, nominative plural oignon)

  1. onion (Allium cepa)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Angevin: ognon, ugnon
  • ⇒ Bourbonnais-Berrichon: ognounet
  • Bourguignon: ougnion
  • Champenois: ègnon, ognon, ongnon, ougnon
  • Franc-Comtois: agnon, ègnon, onon, ognon, ougnon, ounon
    Jurassien Franc-Comtois: oégnon, ouégnon, ouignon
  • Middle French: oingnon
    • French: oignon, ognon (post-1990 spelling)
      • Saint Dominican Creole French: z'oignon
        • Haitian Creole: zonyon
      • Seychellois Creole: zonyon
  • Gallo: ongnon
  • Lorrain: ougnan
    Vosgien: ègnon, èyon
  • Norman: ougnoun, ouongnon
  • Picard: ongnon
  • Poitevin-Saintongeais: egnun, ignun, ougnun
  • Walloon: agnon
  • → Middle Breton: oingnon
    • Breton: ognon
  • → Middle Dutch: ayuun, ejuun, oinjun
    • Dutch: ajuin (see there for further descendants)
  • → Middle Dutch: uyen
    • Dutch: ui (see there for further descendants)
    • Limburgish: ooj, un
  • → Middle English: onyoun
    • English: onion (see there for further descendants)
  • →? Middle Irish: uinniún
    • Irish: oinniún
  • → Welsh: wynwyn
